additional_info.subject: RE: ID0455361-DC/Si-D/AT-[MP/S5 170003627] Charging voltage issue CRM:02889000729
additional_info.body:
Dear colleagues,
We have reviewed the logs from the failed charging attempt in Pettneu on Saturday evening, October 11th. The session terminated unexpectedly with a State B, and the error EVSuspended was recorded.
Upon further analysis, we observed that during the pre-charge phase, the voltage only reached 149V, which is below the required threshold. As a result, the vehicle aborted the session due to insufficient voltage.
Please find attached the Excel file containing our investigation details. Based on the findings, we recommend that the local team go onsite to inspect the contactors and voltage transducers.
Additionally, we would appreciate it if you could organize a live remote session with the debug station so we can assist further and verify the setup in real time.
Let us know your availability.
With best regards,
Guilherme Andre De Verissimo Dias
Siemens S.A.
SI E CS SD L3
201, Avenida 25 de Abril
2845-547, Corroios, Portugal

additional_info.subject: RE: AW: ID0455361-DC/Si-D/AT-[MP/S5 170003627] Charging voltage issue CRM:02889000729
additional_info.body:
Dear Johannes,
Thank you for your continued collaboration on this case!
Following up on our live debug session last Friday, we noted that the specific error we were investigating could not be reproduced at that time.
However, we've been diligently monitoring the charging sessions since then. Over the last three days, out of a total of 24 sessions, we observed two instances where the charge was 0kW. Upon reviewing these, the reason identified was "Authorization invalid."
We also want to clarify an observation regarding the "no PLC link." This indicates that the EV encountered an issue transmitting a part of the SLAC (Power Line Communication) process, which is crucial for communication between the EVSE (Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment) and the EV.
During the SLAC communication phase, there are three primary active components:
EcoG
CCS
EV
To enhance the communication reliability and performance, we recommend troubleshooting and ensuring that all these components are operating at their best. A practical step we suggest is to clean the plug, as this can sometimes improve communication quality.
Please don't hesitate to reach out if you need further assistance or want to discuss next steps.
With best regards,
Guilherme Andre De Verissimo Dias
Siemens S.A.
SI E CS SD L3
201, Avenida 25 de Abril
2845-547, Corroios, Portugal

additional_info.subject: 0455361 - ID0455361-DC/Si-D/AT-[MP/S5 170003627] Charging voltage issue CRM:00472000464
additional_info.body:
Dear Johannes,
I was reviewing this case and looking for the past weeks to see if any major issue was happening.
Most of the charging sessions are being ended from P07, this shows us that the general condition from the charger is good.
Also the event reported before, failure in the PRE_CHARGE phase was not present in the last 4 weeks.
The "NO PLC COMMUNICATION LINK" we already discussed before and it's not a clear indication from a fault in the charger and more a unsuccessful authentication.
I suggest to close the ticket since I don't see any problem in the charger. Let me know if you agree or if you need any other clarification.
With best regards,
